body: Tested locally, it works as expected. This makes sense to have for things like crosshairs with adjustable sizes, as you'll want them to be affected both by oversampling and the user preference. (You could downscale a high-resolution crosshair, but this won't look as good as having the SVG directly rasterized at the display resolution.) **Testing project:** [test_pr_109740.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21845322/test_pr_109740.zip) *Drag the slider to adjust the crosshair size. Try multiple window sizes too.* I noticed some issues though: - This seems to break editor icon scaling. See the CheckButton icon in the Project Settings for instance: - `size_override` should be exposed as a property, since it now has a both a setter and getter exposed: - I didn't find a way to preserve `canvas_items` oversampling behavior *and* allow for custom size adjustments in the above demo. It works OK without oversampling (at the default window size), but at larger window sizes, the crosshair becomes blurry. I've tried to use `get_viewport().get_stretch_transform().get_scale()` to no avail (it made the crosshair too large *and* blurry).
